prompt: What is the owner's full name?
help: The legal owner of the property or building (a person or a company). This is the party who will sign the form.

prompt: Is someone acting for the owner (an architect, engineer, contractor or consultant)? If so, who?
help: The form has a separate field for the owner's representative. Leave blank if the owner is applying directly.

prompt: What mailing address and email should the Safety Codes Officer use to reach you?
help: Used for requests for more information and for the decision. Give a full mailing address and one monitored email.

prompt: Email address for correspondence
help: One email address that is checked regularly.

prompt: What date are you submitting this request?
help: Today's date unless you plan to submit later.

prompt: Which municipality or authority is reviewing the building permit?
help: This sets the local overlay (form recipient, local guides). The demonstration topic is built around Edmonton.

prompt: Is this request for a whole jurisdiction instead of one site?
help: Tick yes only if the variance is not tied to a single property. Most project variances are site-specific, so answer no.

prompt: What is the building permit number (if you have one yet)?
help: A variance must be tied to a building permit. If you have not applied yet, leave this blank and say so; Calgary states a variance number cannot be issued without a building permit number.

prompt: What is the municipal (street) address of the site?
help: The full street address as it appears on the building permit.

prompt: Do you have the legal land description (lot, block, plan)?
help: Found on the land title or tax notice. Lot, block and plan describe a city lot.

prompt: Block and plan numbers
help: Block and plan from the land title.

prompt: Plan number
help: The registered plan number from the land title.

prompt: Do you have the Alberta Township Survey (ATS) description (quarter, section, township, range, meridian)?
help: Mostly used for rural land. Leave blank for a city lot with lot, block and plan.

prompt: Section, township, range, meridian
help: Enter the section, township, range and meridian from the ATS description (fill each if known).

prompt: In your own words, what do you want to build or do differently?
help: Describe the project in a few sentences, for example: a six-storey apartment building with one exit stair.

prompt: What is the building used for (occupancy)?
help: For example apartments or condominiums (residential), offices, shops. Apartments are the residential occupancy.

prompt: How many storeys is the building (building height)?
help: Count the floors above ground. The Edmonton guide covers residential buildings of 6 storeys or less.

prompt: What is the building area in square metres?
help: The footprint area of the largest floor, from your drawings.

prompt: How many dwelling units are on each floor?
help: The Edmonton guide covers not more than 4 units per floor served by one exit stair.

prompt: Is the building sprinklered throughout?
help: Fully sprinklered means automatic sprinklers in the whole building. Answer unknown if not decided.

prompt: Is this a new building or a renovation of an existing one?
help: Choose new for new construction, renovation for work in an existing building.

prompt: What is the main code requirement you want to do differently?
help: For the demo topic this is the requirement to provide at least two exits from a floor area. Say it plainly; the tool will find the article.

prompt: Describe your proposed alternative in plain words.
help: What you will do instead of the second exit (for example one exit stair with added protection). Do not claim it is safe or equal; just say what you propose.

prompt: Which protective measures will you add (mitigations)?
help: List what you plan, for example stair enclosure and fire separation, smoke control, sprinklers, fire department access. Pick from the catalogue in the next screen or add your own.

prompt: Do you already have reports, drawings, standards or listings that support the proposal?
help: List names and dates (for example a fire protection engineer's report). These are attached in Section D.

prompt: Which registered professional (architect or engineer) is involved?
help: Edmonton requires registered architect and/or engineers for a Point Access Block. Give name and firm, or say none yet.

prompt: Is a qualified Fire Protection or Life Safety Code Consultant preparing the Alternative Solution?
help: Edmonton requires the Alternative Solution for a Point Access Block to be prepared by one. If no, the tool stops and tells you what is needed.

prompt: Have you booked or held a pre-application meeting with the City?
help: Recommended by Edmonton for Point Access Block proposals. Optional but helpful.
